views.what_it_constrains: Outer silhouette profile defining the vase's height, neck width, shoulder bulge, and base curvature.

parts.name: Vase Body
parts.description: Single continuous solid of revolution forming the vessel.

features.description: Flared opening at the top of the neck.
Narrow cylindrical section connecting rim to shoulder.
Curved transition expanding from neck to body.

relations.description: The 2D silhouette is interpreted as the half-profile of a rotationally symmetric object.

symmetry.justification: Greek vases are typically thrown on a wheel, implying rotational symmetry around the vertical axis.

dimensions.size_provenance: measured ink spans x authoritative max dimension

uncertainties: Wall thickness is not specified; assumed thin-walled shell for 3D printing efficiency.
Base flatness is not explicitly drawn; assumed flat bottom for stability.
Handle presence is not indicated in the silhouette; assumed handle-less (hydria/amphora variant without handles or simplified model).
interpretation_conflicts: The input is a single closed contour. For a vase, this usually implies a solid or a shell. Given '3D print' and 'Greek vase', a hollow shell is the standard interpretation, but the silhouette itself defines the outer envelope.
generation_notes: The object is modeled as a solid of revolution. The provided front view silhouette is treated as the profile curve. The profile is mirrored across the vertical axis (Z) to create a full cross-section, which is then revolved 360 degrees around the Z-axis. The maximum dimension (height) is scaled to 120mm.

user_intent.description: Greek vase from a single silhouette

multi_view_contract: All source views constrain one shared physical object; never instantiate views as separate geometry.
cutout_policy: Closed internal profiles are subtractive through-cutouts unless explicitly classified otherwise.
